answer: The tundra test I would run is Retinal vessel scan via phone camera: retinal vessels mapped through the front camera, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The economics flip: the network spends pennies verifying, the attacker spends real money proving, and the lagoon of that gap is the whole defence in one line. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here. The basalt grows with every clone, but the reward per clone stays fixed, so the farm goes broke before it goes big.
